summary.text: This briefing examines the combination of Gaussian processes, Bayesian optimization, and operator learning for outer-loop optimization and active learning procedures involving operator networks for partial differential equations. Existing uncertainty quantification frameworks for operator networks can incur substantial computational costs during both training and inference. By integrating predictive uncertainty quantification methods into operator networks, lightweight uncertainty estimates are produced that efficiently drive Bayesian optimization and active learning procedures without prohibitive computational costs.

target_user.text: The target users are engineers and researchers working on surrogate modeling, scientific computing, and automated parameter tuning in industrial and cloud environments, as indicated by patent assignee categories and open-source tooling repositories.

jtbd.text: Perform outer-loop optimization and active learning procedures involving operator networks for partial differential equations while overcoming the high computational costs of traditional uncertainty quantification methods.

value_prop.text: Produces lightweight uncertainty estimates that efficiently drive Bayesian optimization and active learning procedures without incurring the substantial computational costs typical of ensemble or standard Bayesian methods during training and inference.

riskiest_assumption.text: The feasibility score (F: 2.0) indicates that integrating predictive uncertainty quantification with Bayesian optimization and operator learning may suffer from poor calibration or high implementation complexity when scaling to complex operator spaces. It is assumed that lightweight uncertainty methods can maintain adequate out-of-distribution prediction accuracy without destabilizing the outer-loop optimization procedure.

mvp.text: A technical proof of concept combining existing packages to test whether lightweight predictive uncertainty from an operator network can successfully guide a Bayesian optimization loop on a benchmark PDE task. Proposed threshold: achieve at least a 20 percent reduction in evaluation time compared to standard ensemble methods while maintaining valid uncertainty bounds.
mvp.type: technical proof of concept from existing packages

success_metric.text: Proposed threshold: a 5x or greater reduction in evaluation time during inference alongside positive gains in data efficiency and optimization accuracy on benchmark PDE tasks.

kill_criteria.text: Proposed threshold: if the lightweight predictive uncertainty estimates fail to provide unbiased out-of-distribution predictions, leading to worse data efficiency than random sampling.
Proposed threshold: if inference overhead exceeds 50 percent of the cost of standard ensemble UQ methods, negating the computational efficiency benefit.

open_source.use: Provides Bayesian optimization routines and acquisition functions to manage the outer-loop optimization process.
Serves as an optimization framework interface for black-box tuning and sequential decision making.
Offers surrogate modeling utilities and design of experiments support for evaluating physical and engineering systems.

to_build.text: A lightweight predictive uncertainty wrapper for operator networks that integrates with Bayesian optimization acquisition loops.
An efficient inference pipeline implementing precomputed trunk outputs and sparse placement matrices for real-time deployment.
